items.text: Ukraine’s parliament has approved a new law that aims to facilitate the recruitment of new soldiers. Under this law, all men aged between 18 and 60 are required to carry documents confirming their registration with the military. Additionally, the law offers incentives such as cash bonuses and financial assistance for housing or vehicles to soldiers. The government emphasized the urgent need for new troops because there may be a shortage of personnel in certain areas. However, serving troops received disappointing news. A clause that specifies time limits on their service was removed from the law. This is particularly upsetting for soldiers engaged in combat since the beginning of the conflict. The decision not to include provisions for demobilization after a specified period has left many soldiers feeling uncertain about their future. Difficult words: facilitate (to make something possible or easier), incentive (motivation or reward offered to encourage someone to do something), demobilization (discharging soldiers from military service). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ukraine needs more soldiers. Especially in some areas, there may not be enough soldiers soon. Ukraine’s parliament passed a new law which will make it easier to recruit new soldiers. The law says that all men aged 18 to 60 must carry papers which show that they joined the military . The law also offers rewards like money or help to buy a house or car. But there is bad news for the soldiers who are already serving . The new law doesn’t say how long they will serve. Before the new law, soldiers could stop their service after three years. Now, they can’t. This makes things hard for soldiers fighting since the start of the war. Difficult words: recruit (to put someone on the list in the military), military (soldiers), serve (to work for another person or organization). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ukraine needs more soldiers. In some places, there will not be enough soldiers soon. Ukraine’s parliament makes a new law . This law is about soldiers. All men from 18 to 60 years old must have papers with them. These papers say that they are in the army . The law gives extra money and things to soldiers. They get help to buy a house or car. Soldiers who fight since the beginning of the war are not happy. Before the law, they can stop after three years of fighting. This is not true anymore. They cannot choose to stop fighting. Difficult words: law (an official rule), army (soldiers), extra (more). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In a significant escalation of tensions in the Middle East, Iran initiated a large-scale drone and missile attack on Israel on Saturday night. This action is seen as a response to an earlier attack on the Iranian consulate in Damascus by Israel. Israel is currently on high alert, with its armed forces fully prepared and its air defenses active. Jordan has also declared a state of emergency in response to the situation. President Biden has returned to the White House for urgent discussions with his national security advisers. The attack raises concerns about the potential for further escalation and the risk of a broader regional conflict. Difficult words: escalation (an increase in intensity or seriousness), large-scale (involving large numbers or a large area), consulate (an office that represents a country in another country). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Saturday night, Iran used drones and rockets to attack Israel. Iran said that the attack was an answer to Israel’s attack on Iran’s consulate in Damascus earlier this month. Israeli soldiers were ready for the attack and they managed to withstand the attack with the help of other countries, for example, the US, UK, and Jordan. Jordan also said there was an emergency in the country. US President Biden was back at the White House for quick talks with his security team. People worry that things could get even worse and there might be a big fight in the area. The situation in the Middle East was serious already before the attack. Difficult words: consulate (an office for people of a country in another country), withstand (to stay the same after something serious happens), emergency (a serious or dangerous situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Saturday night, Iran attacks Israel. Iran uses many drones and rockets. Iran does this because Israel attacks its office in Damascus before. Israel expects the attack. Israeli soldiers are ready. Other countries help them, for example, the US, UK and Jordan. They destroy the drones and rockets. Nobody is hurt. Jordan is in an emergency now. Another attack may happen. The situation in the Middle East is already serious before the attack. The attack makes the area even more unsafe . People worry that things will get worse. Difficult words: expect (to think or believe that something will happen), destroy (to damage something very badly), unsafe (not safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Eid al-Fitr, a festival that marks the end of Ramadan, was celebrated globally with prayers, family reunions, and festive activities. However, the ongoing war in Gaza cast a shadow over the holiday for many Muslims. Despite the festive atmosphere, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and the threat of Israel’s ground offensive in Rafah dampened the celebrations. Turkey’s President Erdogan expressed support for Gaza, and he emphasized the need for peace and tranquility . Similar sentiments were echoed in Kenya and Indonesia. In Malaysia, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim called for unity and respect among diverse groups. While joyous, the celebrations were marked by awareness of the ongoing crisis in Gaza, highlighting the importance of solidarity and compassion. Difficult words: cast a shadow (to cause something to be less good or enjoyable), dampen (to make it less strong or intense), tranquility (a peaceful, calm state), sentiment (a view or opinion). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Muslims in the world celebrated Eid al-Fitr, the festival which marks the end of Ramadan. But people didn’t enjoy the festival as much as they normally do because of the conflict in Gaza. Leaders in Turkey, Kenya, and Indonesia expressed support for Gaza and called for peace . In Malaysia, different groups expressed unity and respect. Although people celebrated, the conflict-affected their mood. For many people, it is important to remember the bad things happening in the world. They believe that it is important to be kind and support each other in difficult times. Difficult words: support (help), peace (when there is no war), unity (when people are as one). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People all over the world celebrate Eid al-Fitr. It is a special holiday after Ramadan. People pray . It is the time when everyone is happy. But this year, people are sad. They remember the fighting in Gaza. Leaders in Turkey, Kenya, and Indonesia support Gaza. They want the fighting to end. In Malaysia, leaders say that everyone should be friends and respect each other. People have fun celebrating. But they are sad at the same time. They want to help. It is important to be kind and stick together when times are difficult. Difficult words: pray (to talk to God), respect (to be nice and fair to others), stick together (to stay close to each other). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Peter Higgs, the Nobel Prize-winning physicist known as the father of the ‘God particle’, has passed away at the age of 94. He gained fame for his groundbreaking theory in the 1960s, proposing the existence of the Higgs boson, a particle responsible for giving mass to other particles and binding the universe together. Decades later, the theory was confirmed by experiments at the Large Hadron Collider in Cern, Switzerland. Higgs’ humility and dedication to science were notable, as he shied away from the term ‘God particle’ despite its popular usage. He helped unravel one of the greatest enigmas in physics which earned him a place alongside names like Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein. The discovery of the Higgs boson was a significant achievement in physics that contributed to our understanding of fundamental particles and forces in the universe. Difficult words: unravel (to make something known or understood), enigma (mystery or puzzle), fundamental (basic). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Peter Higgs is a famous physicist who won the Nobel Prize. Last week, he died at the age of 94. People know Higgs for his theory which suggests the existence of the Higgs boson, often called the ‘God particle’. According to Higgs this particle gives mass to other particles and plays an important role in creating the universe. Higgs developed this theory in the 1960s, and decades later, scientists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland proved it. Although people normally used the term ‘God particle’, Higgs was a modest person and he focused on science. Finding the Higgs boson was a big discovery which helped scientists understand particles and forces in the universe. Difficult words: theory (ideas which explain something), mass (many particles together which form one body), prove (to show that something is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Peter Higgs is a famous scientist. He wins the Nobel Prize. He dies last week at the age of 94. Higgs speaks about the Higgs boson. People often call the Higgs boson the ‘God particle ’. This particle gives mass to other particles. It holds the universe together. This is what Higgs believes. Other scientists prove it at CERN in Switzerland many years later. Higgs is a humble man. Only science is important to him. He does not want to be famous. Finding the Higgs boson is a big thing. Thanks to it, we understand the universe much better. Difficult words: particle (a very small piece of something), mass (many small things together), prove (to show that something is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The victory of Social Democrat Peter Pellegrini in Slovakia’s presidential election has strengthened the ruling party led by Robert Fico. Fico’s party is seen as eurosceptic and aligned with Russian narratives, and it’ll now have both the government and the president from the same political spectrum. Pellegrini’s campaign focused on promising stability for the government if elected, as he is a key coalition leader. He pledged not to hinder the government’s agenda. His opponent Ivan Korčok accused Pellegrini of risking Slovakia’s involvement in the war by supporting Ukraine. However, Pellegrini hasn’t yet clearly defined his stance on various issues. Pellegrini expresses pro-European sentiments, but he also emphasizes protecting Slovakian interests. Pellegrini’s win with 54% of the vote raises concerns about Slovakia’s future alignment with populist trends, similar to Hungary under Viktor Orbán. Difficult words: hinder (to make it difficult for someone to do something or for something to happen), stance (attitude), alignment (being in agreement or coordination with). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Peter Pellegrini became Slovakia’s new president, which supported Robert Fico’s ruling party. Fico’s party is skeptical towards the EU and it prefers Russian views. Now, both the government and the president are from the same political spectrum , and many people believe that it will make the country stable. Pellegrini promised to support the government. His opponent Ivan Korčok criticized Pellegrini. Kročok said that Slovakia could get involved in in war with Russia. For some people, Pellegrini’s political ideas are not clear. He agrees with the EU but at the same time, he wants to protect Slovakian interests. Some people worry that Slovakia will follow the same path as Hungary. Difficult words: skeptic (when you doubt that something is true, good, and so on), political spectrum (political opinions which exist), opponent (someone who competes in a contest or game). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Slovakia has a new president. Peter Pellegrini wins the election . Pellegrini has similar ideas to Robert Fico. Fico is Slovakia’s Prime Minister. He is skeptical about the EU. He likes Russian ideas more. Now, both the president and the government have the same ideas. Some people believe that it is good for the country. Ivan Kročok is the other candidate for president. He is afraid that Slovakia will take part in war with Russia. Pellegrini says that he agrees with the EU. But Slovakia and its people are more important. Some people worry that Slovakia will be more populist , just like Hungary. Difficult words: election (when people vote for a person in politics), skeptical (when you do not believe that something is true or real), populist (ideas interesting for ordinary people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Rapidly melting snow resulted in rivers reaching record-high levels and caused severe flooding in Russia and Kazakhstan. More than 100,000 people have been ordered to evacuate. The floodwaters have overwhelmed settlements in various regions, including the Ural Mountains and Siberia. Officials are urging caution and immediate evacuation in affected areas. In Orenburg, the Ural River surpassed critical levels and prompted authorities to issue evacuation warnings. Emergency measures such as reinforcing dams and embankments are underway. The flood situation remains challenging as water levels are still rising. President Putin and President Tokayev of Kazakhstan discussed the severity of the situation, and they stated that significant portions of both countries were affected by flooding. Difficult words: reinforce (to support), embankment (a wall built to prevent a river from flooding an area), severity (seriousness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Russia and Kazakhstan are evacuating over 100,000 people. Melting snow caused severe flooding in both countries. The flooding affected regions like the Ural Mountains and Siberia where rivers overflew at record levels. Officials evacuated people in flooded areas like Orenburg, where the Ural River exceeded critical levels. Workers are supporting dams, but the situation remains serious. Water levels in some regions are still rising. Presidents Putin and Tokayev discussed the situation. They said that there were floods in large parts of both countries. Difficult words: melt (when snow or ice turns into water), severe (serious), exceed (to be more than or over a limit). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Snow melts in mountains in Russia and Kazakhstan. There is too much water in rivers. There are floods in both countries. The situation is serious. More than 100,000 people must leave their homes. It is not safe to stay. Water in rivers rises too much. The floods have an impact on areas like the Ural Mountains and Siberia. Officials say that people must leave quickly. Workers support dams . But the flood situation is still serious. Presidents Putin and Tokayev talk about how bad the flooding is. They say that floods are in many parts of both countries. Difficult words: melt (when snow or ice turns into water), flood (when water from a river gets into people’s homes), dam (a wall across a river which stops the flow and keeps water in one place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A rare earthquake struck New Jersey, and it caused buildings in New York City and nearby areas to shake. The United States Geological Survey reported the quake’s magnitude as 4.8, with its epicenter just northeast of Whitehouse Station, New Jersey. The earthquake occurred around 10:20 local time and it didn’t cause major damage. A UN Security Council meeting in New York was briefly halted due to the tremor . Eyewitnesses reported feeling the quake across the city, with buildings shaking for about 15 to 20 seconds. Although they are rare, earthquakes have occurred in New York in the past, with the most recent one in January of the same year. Despite the interest generated by the event, it isn’t expected to pose a serious risk to residents. Difficult words: halt (to stop), tremor (a slight earthquake). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A rare earthquake hit New Jersey. It caused buildings in New York City and nearby areas to shake . The earthquake had a magnitude of 4.8. It occurred around 10:20 local time. Luckily, it didn’t cause big damage. A UN Security Council paused a meeting in New York because of the earthquake. People said that they could feel the shaking for about 15 to 20 seconds. Earthquakes are not usual in New York, but they happened before. The most recent one happened in January 2024. It surprised many, but experts believe it will not have a big impact on local people. Difficult words: shake (to move quickly from side to side), magnitude (a number which says how strong an earthquake is), recent (happening not long ago). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An earthquake happens in New Jersey. Buildings in New York City move too. Earthquakes are not usual on the east coast of the United States. The earthquake happens around 10:20 in the morning. Nothing serious happens. Nobody is hurt. No buildings fall. People at a UN meeting feel the ground move. They stop the meeting for a short time. Some people in New York say they feel the ground move for about 15 to 20 seconds. Earthquakes are not usual in New York. But they happen here before. People are interested in the event but it is not a big problem for anyone. Difficult words: earthquake (when the ground moves), serious (bad or very important). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Latin American governments, including influential countries like Brazil, stood by Mexico after its embassy in Ecuador was raided. The raid aimed to arrest Jorge Glas, Ecuador’s former vice president, who had sought asylum in Mexico. The arrest was carried out on Friday night, and it led Mexico to suspend relations with Ecuador. Ecuador argued that asylum protections were invalid due to Glas’s corruption charges; however, embassies are considered sovereign territory under international law. Governments across Latin America criticized the arrest, and Brazil called it a violation of diplomatic norms. Mexico said that it would appeal to international bodies for the violation of its embassy’s immunity. Meanwhile, US officials called for dialogue to resolve the dispute, and they emphasized strict compliance with international treaties . Difficult words: asylum (the protection granted by a state to someone who has left their home country as a political refugee), suspend (to temporarily stop), treaty (a formal deal between states). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Latin American countries, including Brazil, supported Mexico after an attack on its embassy in Ecuador. The attack aimed to arrest Jorge Glas, Ecuador’s former vice president, who sought refuge in Mexico. Mexico interrupted relations with Ecuador, and they called the arrest wrong and against international rules. Even though Ecuador argued, that embassies are protected places. Many Latin American governments criticized the arrest. Brazil said that it broke diplomatic rules. Mexico will ask international groups for help. US officials asked for talks to solve the problem and follow international rules. Difficult words: embassy (the official office of people who represent their country in a foreign country), aim (to plan), refuge (protection). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is an attack Mexican embassy in Ecuador. Latin American countries, including Brazil, support Mexico. Jorge Glas is Ecuador’s former vice president . He stays at the embassy. That is why the attack happens. Mexico stopped talking to Ecuador after the attack. Mexico says that nobody can attack an embassy. Many countries in Latin America say that the attack is not right. Ecuador breaks the rules for how countries should act with each other. Mexico will ask for help from other countries. US officials ask the countries to talk about the problem and follow international rules. Difficult words: embassy (an office for people who represent their country in another country), vice president (an official below a president), international (between countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Football star Lionel Messi has taken a stand against climate change and he teamed up with an environmental organization Join the Planet. Messi wants to extend his impact beyond sports by participating in efforts to protect the environment. His collaboration involves cleaning up coastlines worldwide and transforming collected plastics into a sculpture that resembles his iconic left football boot. This initiative begins with cleaning the Paraná River in Rosario, Argentina. The director of Join the Planet Foundation expressed optimism about Messi’s involvement, and he emphasized Messi’s ability to influence global culture positively. Messi’s sculpture is made from recycled materials and highlights the importance of sustainability. Messi believes that collective effort and community spirit can safeguard the planet. Join the Planet repurposes discarded materials to fund projects that preserve natural ecosystems globally. Difficult words: take a stand (to express an opinion), resemble (to look like), repurpose (to find a new use for an idea, product, or building). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Lionel Messi is a famous Argentine footballer. He joined forces with an environmental organization Join the Planet to fight climate change. Messi wants to use his influence and he will take part in environmental projects. He plans to clean up beaches and change collected plastics into a sculpture of his football boot. This effort begins with cleaning the Paraná River in Rosario, Argentina. Join the Planet is excited about Messi’s help. People in the world know Messi, and his help can have a big impact on people and how they think about climate change. Messi believes that if all people get together, they can save the planet. Difficult words: join forces (to work together), influence (impact), effort (activity to achieve something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lionel Messi is a famous footballer from Argentina. He wants to help the planet. He works with an environmental organization now. He wants to clean up the planet. He helps collect plastics and clean beaches. Messi wants to inspire others to care for the planet. Messi is so famous that people may listen to him. The first project is cleaning the Paraná River in Argentina. People are excited about Messi’s help. It can change things. Messi believes that if people work together, it can make a big change. We all must try to save our planet. Difficult words: environmental organization (group of people who work to protect the natural world), inspire (to make someone want to do something because I do it), excited (happy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The EU created the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) to help member states recover from the COVID-19 pandemic’s economic and social effects. The RRF is part of the NextGenerationEU plan, and with 723 billion euros allocated, it offers grants or loans to EU members. Grants finance green and digital projects and strengthen economies, while loans support recovery efforts. However, the RRF is temporary and it’ll end in 2026. It complements other EU recovery measures . COVID-19 hit industries differently, particularly those reliant on personal contact, like tourism and retail. SMEs faced challenges like late payments and supply chain disruptions. Job losses affected vulnerable groups and highlighted broader labor market impacts. Difficult words: resilience (the capability to recover), complement (to emphasize or improve the qualities of something), measure (a plan or course of action taken to achieve a particular purpose). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The EU made a plan called the RR to help countries after COVID-19. They gave 723 billion euros for it. The RRF gives money to countries as grants or loans . Grants help with green and digital projects and loans help with recovery . But the RRF will end in 2026. It works together with other EU plans. COVID-19 hurt some businesses a lot. Especially those where personal contact is important, like tourism and shops. Small businesses had problems like late payments and not enough things to sell. Some people lost jobs, especially those with less education. The RRF tries to help EU countries and people after COVID-19. Difficult words: grant (money which a company or person gets for free), loan (money which someone lends to someone else), recovery (when things return to a normal state). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The EU makes a big plan called the RRF. It helps EU countries after COVID-19. They give 723 billion euros for it. The RRF gives money to countries to help them. The RRF is only for countries which are in the EU. Some of the money is free . These are called grants. Countries need not pay this money back. The RRF also gives loans. A loan is money which you must pay back. The RRF will end in 2026. It works together with other EU plans. COVID-19 hurts some businesses a lot, like tourism and shops. Small businesses have problems like late payments . Some people lose their jobs. It is important to help countries and people after COVID-19. Difficult words: free (something what does not cost any money), tourism (businesses which help people travel), payment (paying someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A recent study by a market intelligence firm Caliber found that fewer people in the United States are considering buying a Tesla car. One reason for this is said to be the behavior of Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla, who some people find controversial . Despite Tesla’s previous strong sales growth, it’s expected to report poor sales soon. The study showed that people’s interest in buying a Tesla car decreased from November 2021 to February 2024. At the same time, people’s interest in buying cars from traditional companies like Mercedes, BMW, and Audi slightly increased. The study also found that most Americans connect Tesla’s reputation with Elon Musk. Marketing experts say that controversies about Musk’s political beliefs and public statements are affecting Tesla’s brand and demand. Additionally, economic worries and competition from other companies like BYD from China are also putting pressure on Tesla. Difficult words: controversial (causing disagreement or discussion), reputation (the beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something), controversy (a public disagreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A recent study found that fewer people in the United States want to buy a Tesla car. One reason for this is the behavior of Elon Musk who is the CEO of Tesla. Some people don’t like him. In the past, Tesla’s sales grew, but experts expect lower sales soon. The study showed that since November 2021, people got less interested in Tesla. They got more interested in buying cars from companies like Mercedes, BMW, and Audi. Most Americans think of Elon Musk when they think about Tesla. This is a problem because Musk’s ideas and statements are affecting Tesla’s brand and sales. Also, worries about money and competition from other companies are making things hard for Tesla. Difficult words: behavior (the way someone acts), statement (what someone says openly), brand (a product which a company makes under a particular name). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A study says that fewer people in the US want a Tesla car now. One reason is Elon Musk. Elon Musk is the boss of Tesla. Some people do not like him. People do not agree with things which he says. Tesla sells well in the past. But it may change soon. People are not so much interested in Tesla these days. For many people, Tesla is Elon Musk. They now think about buying cars from other companies like Mercedes, BMW, and Audi. Experts say that Musk hurts Tesla’s sales . The company has also problems with money and with carmakers from China. Difficult words: hurt (to have a bad impact on someone or something), sale (when a company sells things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police in Finland reported a shooting at Viertola school in Vantaa near the capital Helsinki. The shooting occurred at a primary school with about 800 students. The incident happened in the morning, shortly after classes resumed following the Easter holidays. The police responded swiftly, detained the suspect, and confiscated the firearm. Police confirmed one fatality , and described it as a tragic event. The Finnish Prime Minister expressed shock and sympathy for the victims and their families. Currently, police believe there are no other suspects. Sadly, one of the injured individuals has died. The other two are in critical condition. The situation is still developing, and updates will follow. Difficult words: confiscate (to take someone’s property with authority), fatality (death by accident, in war, or from disease). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a shooting at a school near Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Police said that the shooter was a 12-year-old boy. He hurt three children and ran away when police arrived, but they caught him quickly. Sadly, one child died in the incident. The Finnish Prime Minister said he feels for the victims and their families. The shooting happened in the morning, after the Easter holidays. It happened at a school with about 800 students. The police came quickly, caught the boy, and took away the gun. According to police, there was no other suspect . Difficult words: victim (a hurt or killed person), suspect (the person who others believe did something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A shooting happens in a school near Helsinki, the capital of Finland. It is an elementary school . Small children go there. The shooter is a boy from the school. He is only 12 years old. He hurts three people. One child dies. Police come quickly. The boy runs away. Police catch him. They take his gun. Everyone is shocked . It is a sad day for Finland. Police say that only one boy is the shooter. At the moment, they do not know why he does it. Police must find out. Difficult words: elementary school (a school for children who are between five and thirteen years old), shocked (surprised and upset). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A company in Japan has stopped making baby diapers due to decreased demand and is focusing instead on adult diapers. This highlights a significant issue: Japan’s birth rate hit a new low last year, with more deaths than births. If this trend continues, Japan’s population could decline by 30% in 45 years. To address this, Japan explores futuristic solutions. Jennifer Robertson, an expert on Japanese culture, discusses challenges and government responses, including consideration of robotics. While Japan aimed for a robotic society by 2025, reality differs from early expectations. Efforts to integrate robots into various sectors are challenging. Robertson highlights the complexities of robotics in Japan, including their role in surveillance and data collection, and explores the implications of technology and potential future developments. Difficult words: futuristic (having or involving very modern technology or design), complexity (being difficult to understand or find an answer to), surveillance (the careful watching of a person or place). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A company in Japan stopped making baby diapers because fewer people needed them. Instead of that, they focus on diapers for older people. This shows a big problem. Japan has fewer babies being born and more people dying, so its population might get much smaller. Some experts believe that Japan’s population could drop by 30% in 45 years. Japan is trying new ideas to solve this problem. Jennifer Robertson is an expert on Japan, and he talks about the problems and what the government is doing. The government thought about using robots, but it is not as easy as they thought. Robots in Japan mostly do only simple tasks like entertainment or security. Difficult words: diaper (a thick soft cloth which a baby has between the legs because he or she can’t use the toilet yet), population (people), entertainment (an event or activity which makes others happy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fewer babies are born in Japan every year. One company makes baby diapers . They stop. They start making diapers for older people. It is a better business. The population in Japan is getting older. This is a big problem. More people die and fewer people are born. Experts say that in 45 years, there will be 30% fewer people. Japan is trying to solve this problem. Jennifer Robertson knows a lot about Japan. She talks about what the government is doing. They think about using robots. But it is not as easy as it seems. Robots in Japan mostly do simple tasks . They cannot replace people. People hope that new technology will change things in the future. Difficult words: diaper (a thick soft cloth for babies who cannot use the toilet yet), task (work which you must do), replace (to put one thing or person in place of another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A recent survey revealed that half of Europeans disapprove of the European Union’s migration policy and advocate for stricter border controls. The survey was conducted across 18 member states ahead of the European Parliament elections. It shows that there’s a significant negative opinion on the EU’s handling of irregular migration. 51% of respondents view the EU’s impact on migration policy negatively, while only 16% hold a positive view. The strongest criticism comes from nations like France, Austria, and Hungary. Furthermore, supporters of right-wing and far-right parties express the most stringent views on migration policy. 71% of respondents support reinforced border controls. Difficult words: advocate (to support an idea), stringent (strict, precise), reinforced (made stronger or strengthened). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A recent survey showed that many Europeans are unhappy with the European Union’s migration policy . They want stricter border controls. The survey took place across 18 member states before European Parliament elections. 51% of respondents have a negative opinion of the EU’s impact on migration policy. Only 16% of respondents have a positive view. Countries like France, Austria, and Hungary have the most negative views. People who support right-wing and far-right parties want stronger border controls. The survey shows a general opinion across Europe for tougher migration policies. Difficult words: survey (checking people’s ideas or opinions), policy (ideas or a plan which a government or business follows), respondent (a person who answers questions about a service or product). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new survey says that many Europeans do not like how the European Union solves migration . People want stronger borders. In the survey, 51% of people say that they do not like what the EU does about migration. Many people think that the EU makes migration worse. Only 16% are happy about the situation. People in countries like France, Austria, and Hungary are especially unhappy. People who support right-wing parties want stronger borders. Lots of people across Europe want stricter rules about who can come into their countries. Difficult words: survey (checking what people think), migration (people traveling to a new place or country), support (to agree with an idea). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Japanese authorities have ordered Kobayashi Pharmaceutical to recall three dietary supplements due to their connection to two fatalities and over 100 hospitalizations. These supplements contain red yeast rice and they were supposed to help lower cholesterol. The key ingredient, Beni koji, contains a red mold used in food coloring. Kobayashi Pharmaceutical is investigating a potential link between the products and kidney issues. The recall also affects other products using Beni koji. Kobayashi’s share prices fell after the company voluntarily recalled its supplements. The Health Minister urged the company to share information quickly, and the Ministry of Health cautioned people against using Beni koji products. Difficult words: potential (possible), voluntarily (done willingly), caution (to say something as a warning). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Despite the timing, the ruling emphasizes Belgium’s commitment to civic engagement and ensuring broad participation in the democratic process. According to a recent report, only seven countries worldwide met safe air pollution levels in 2023. The global air pollution crisis is alarming scientists who describe it as a global health catastrophe. The report analyzed data from over 30,000 monitoring stations across 134 countries, and it revealed that fine particulate matter (PM2.5) levels exceeded safe limits in most regions. Among the seven countries that met safe air quality guidelines were Australia, Estonia, Finland, and New Zealand, with Iceland having the cleanest air in Europe. While some European countries showed improvement, many still face significant pollution challenges. The countries with the worst air quality were concentrated in South and Central Asia, home to the top 10 most polluted cities in the world. Bangladesh came first, with PM2.5 more than 15 times higher than the WHO annual guideline. The other countries with the worst air quality were Pakistan, India, Tajikistan, and Burkina Faso. Canada was the most polluted country in North America. It is necessary to deal with this issue to ensure public health and reduce its negative effects on society. Difficult words: fine particular matter (tiny pieces of solid matter or liquid that people can inhale), guideline (a general rule or piece of advice). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: monitoring station (a place with systems which check how many chemicals and other things are in the air), exceed (to go beyond), pollution (when the air, water, or soil gets dirty). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
